title: The Farmer Was Replaced brings its million-selling coding simulator to iOS and Android
summary: Consider this: a million copies sold of a game where you write code to run a farm. I wouldn’t have bet on that, but The Farmer Was Replaced got there, and it’s out now on iOS and Android with its new DLC, The Miner Was Replaced, thrown in. You write short programs in a Python-like language, hit execute, and a drone does the tilling, planting and harvesting based on whatever you wrote. No levels, just a steady run of unlocks and problems, like merging pumpkins into one giant one or hunting for treasure in a hedge maze. And if you already code, you can skip the basics and go straight to running a fleet of drones. ... [MORE]

title: Pokémon Go’s Twilight Wishes boosts Shiny odds and brings back Halloween costumed Pokémon
summary: A sky full of stars would be incomplete without boosted Shiny odds for Staryu and Elgyem. That’s Pokémon Go’s Twilight Wishes for you, an event landing later this month. It sees the in-game décor getting the starry treatment too. Wild encounters include Clefairy, Staryu, Elgyem and maybe a Rockruff, with Shiny versions possible across the lot. Raids are Pikachu in a sun crown or a moon crown at one star, Espeon in a sun scarf and Umbreon in a moon scarf at three, and Mega Beedrill, Houndoom, Sableye and Manectric at the top. ... [MORE]

title: Marvel Contest of Champions puts Doctor Doom in charge with its Empire of Doom Saga
summary: Doctor Doom taking over Marvel Contest of Champions’ fighting menu is the most Doom move. The Empire of Doom Saga takeover brings Latverian theming and monthly intro comics, with a motion comic for part one voiced by Matthew Mercer and part two landing in December, when the game turns 12. Star-Lord this time is Kitty Pryde, a comics swap that doesn’t sound real until you look into it. Peter stepped back as team leader, and she headed into space with the Guardians after falling out with the X-Men. Beast gets a rework, and the Victorious Four, a Fantastic Four who follow Doom without question, join the roster too. ... [MORE]

summary: My.Games have had plenty of interesting releases over the years. But one of the more popular has been their humorous medieval RTS Hustle Castle, which recently celebrated nine years since its launch! Now, it's the perfect time to jump back in, with a new in-game event set to kick off soon. The Viral Adventure, which kicks off on November 5th, is a pretty straightforward anniversary event. You'll meet up with the character Sir Mole and be tasked with completing his challenges in order to gain exclusive rewards. title: Bills Must Be Paid brings incremental, piggy bank-smashing gameplay to mobile, out now
summary: You know, it's a bit of a sad state of affairs that, while in the past video games gave us the fantasy of being skilled martial artists or world-defending space soldiers, nowadays it's just about making money. Well, at the very least, Bills Must be Paid is almost as visceral as the most violent boomer shooter, as it's now available to buy on iOS and Android! You may remember us covering Bills Must Be Paid a little while ago, but for those who don't, here's a quick primer. In Bills Must Be Paid, you have only one objective: smash piggy banks, get money and pay off your bills. To help you out, you'll be able to gain upgrades such as perks and rings, but watch out because you only have a limited well of stamina to draw from, and after that runs out, it's game over. ... [MORE]

title: Waframe's new Tau expansion announces launch date for this winter
summary: It seems as if many games nowadays are promising major, paradigm-shifting expansions. We saw it with RuneScape: Reignited, a semi-standalone version of the hit MMORPG, to bring in a new wave of players. But whereas Jagex eventually had to backpedal on their planned spinoff ecosystem, Digital Extremes' new Warframe: Tau expansion looks set to be a true game-changer. The core selling point of Warframe: Tau is that this is a new, expansive single-player narrative to jump into, that sees the long-dormant Tau sector opened for exploration. The sector itself was already explored in the Old Peace update, but now you'll be able to see what's happened to it in the aeons since. ... [MORE]

title: Silver Palace, the Belle Époque-style ARPG, sets release date for this winter
summary: With so many ARPGs on storefronts these days, a new one can seem a little redundant. But as the debut entry in the genre from Elementa Games, Silver Palace is already shaping up to be an exciting new release. And soon you'll be able to judge for yourself, as Silver Palace is confirmed to land on December 14th for iOS and Android! This means magic and technology intertwine, with brawling melee action accompanied by high-calibre weaponry. ... [MORE]

title: Petit Planet unveils release date for MiHoYo's debut cosy life sim
summary: MiHoYo are stepping out of their comfort zone a bit with the upcoming Petit Planet, a cosy life sim where you take care of your own planetoid. And soon, you'll be able to get your hands on it and give it a go. Petit Planet has been confirmed to launch for iOS and Android on December 4th! Petit Planet sees you take on the role of a Tender, growing and expanding your own mini planetoid. You'll slowly gather a resource called Luca, and when you've created enough, you'll be able to add new life to your planet. Between building, planting, decorating and just enjoying life on your planet, you can explore the vast Starsea and go on adventures to other areas. ... [MORE]

title: Death Stranding Odradek shows us how Kojima's hit series might work on mobile
summary: Death Stranding is, for better or for worse, a quintessentially Kojima game. And it's found a lot of success on virtually every platform, including on mobile. But a newly released prototype app exclusive to a recent gallery could show how else the franchise works on mobile, as Death Stranding Odradek hits iOS and Android! Death Stranding Odradek allows visitors to the Azabudai Hills Gallery, which is hosting the 10th anniversary exhibition for Kojima Productions, to complete a delivery mission and experience the world of Death Stranding through AR. Odradek is named for the device worn on Sam's back in Death Stranding, which provides you with in-game information about the terrain and world around you, as well as warning of the presence of dangerous BTs. ... [MORE]

title: Dungeon Splat! proves that clearing monsters from a dungeon is messy business
summary: If there's one stereotype about fantasy adventurers that's true, it's that they mostly have a 'kill first, ask questions never' policy. Have you ever stopped to wonder if you needed to slaughter that group of Orcs hanging around minding their own business? Me neither. And if violently massacring everything in your path is your thing, then Dungeon Splat is for you! Available now on iOS, Dungeon Splat! pits your intrepid adventurer against a winding dungeon full of enemies. Your job? Simply to clear it out in messy, messy fashion. You simply swipe to send your adventurer hurtling and cleaving through enemies, leaving a spray of comfortably PG neon blood and guts in your wake. ... [MORE]

summary: Back in the day, most games lived and died based on a gimmick - a mechanic or selling point you could sum up in a sentence. Of course, that's quite reductive, but every now and then something comes along that harkens back to that time, such as Copy Cats, which is available to buy now on iOS and Android! The concept of Copy Cats is simple: you play a cat transported into a virtual wood that needs to make their escape. Fortunately, you'll have virtual clones of yourself to help you out. The only problem? These clones don't have a mind of their own, and you'll be controlling both yourself and them, all at once. ... [MORE]

title: Hearth and Hamlet lets you build your kingdom at your own pace, so no pressure, really
summary: Incremental clickers have never really, well, clicked with me, only because it's the rapid clicking that injured my arms in the first place (curse you, tennis elbows). But Hearth and Hamlet does seem to offer something a tad more mellow than any kind of frantic tapping, as it's supposed to be a more relaxing experience where you build your medieval kingdom from scratch.  This incremental citybuilder will have you gathering resources and constructing buildings across lovely pixel-art visuals, with workers you can assign to make your settlement thrive. Of course, while it's all nice and cosy at the beginning, you're still running a kingdom, so you'll need to manage morale and handle civic decisions too. Plus, there's the omnipresent tax system to navigate - there's no escaping those, even in the virtual world, it seems. ... [MORE]

title: Leafy Corner lets you flex your green thumb and give virtual plants some TLC
summary: I've always wanted to be like those cool herb-savvy cooks who can grow their own produce in the kitchen, but alas, plants have never really taken a liking to me. Leafy Corner at least helps me care for (or at least attempt to care for) digital flora, as it's coming to mobile in 2027. I say 2027 like it's some sort of faraway future, but I just realised upon writing this that that's only two months away, isn't it? title: StarVaders lets you pilot a mech against aliens using replayable decks, and maybe even rewind time too

The hand-drawn feel of the art style adds to its overall charm in my opinion, and since you get to fend off an alien invasion at that, it's already got my attention from the get-go. Basically, you pilot a cool mech to repel said hostile invaders across a grid-based battlefield, and as you might expect, you'll really need to put your tactical thinking to the test if you want to gain the upper hand. There are all sorts of satisfying combos to chain together to really ramp up the exhilaration of a well-thought-out move. title: Cages: Hidden Worlds is a puzzling, quirky adventure where you escape a forgotten freak show
summary: It's been a big day for mobile announcements, with the likes of Planet of Lana II and Darkest Dungeon II, among others, all set to make their way to mobile. But there're also a few lesser-known, hidden gems buried amongst the announcements, such as the unnerving little puzzle adventure Cages: Hidden Worlds that's set to launch in 2027. The best way to describe Cages: Hidden Worlds is via my initial impression, which is that this is a point-and-click adventure if it were made by Tim Burton. Set in a mysterious mansion packed with the remains of an abandoned freak show and its imprisoned inhabitants, Cages: Hidden Worlds tasks you with solving complex and esoteric puzzles as you attempt to make your escape. ...
